Medical Devices; Ear, Nose, and Throat Devices; Classification of the External Mechanical Stimulator for the Relief of Congestion
records.actor: Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration
records.sourceText: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is classifying the external mechanical stimulator for the relief of congestion into class II (special controls). The special controls that apply to the device type are identified in this order and will be part of the codified language for classification of the external mechanical stimulator for the relief of congestion. We are taking this action because we have determined that classifying the device into class II will provide a reasonable assurance of the safety and effectiveness of the device. We believe this action will also enhance patients' access to beneficial innovative devices, in part by reducing regulatory burdens.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; Dassault Aviation Airplanes
records.sourceText: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-15-04, which applies to certain Dassault Aviation Model FALCON 7X airplanes. AD 2024-15-04 requires revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-15- 04, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would continue to require certain actions in AD 2024-15-04 and would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.sourceText: This action proposes to establish a Class E airspace area extending upwards from 700 feet above the surface of the earth at Shelter Cove Airport (K0Q5), Shelter Cove, CA. K0Q5 is transitioning from a visual flight rules (VFR) to an instrument flight rules (IFR) airport. Additionally, this action would establish a controlled airspace area for the airport, providing coverage to arriving IFR aircraft descending below 1,500 feet above the surface and departing IFR aircraft until reaching 1,200 feet above the surface.

records.actor: Commerce Department; National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
records.sourceText: NMFS solicits nominations for the Atlantic Highly Migratory Species (HMS) Advisory Panel (AP). NMFS consults with and considers the comments and views of the HMS AP when preparing and implementing fishery management plans (FMPs) or FMP amendments for Atlantic swordfish, sharks, tunas, and billfish. Nominations are being sought to fill approximately one third (10) of the seats on the HMS AP, each with a 3-year appointment. The regulations and other materials affected by this format change have all been previously submitted by the State of California and approved by the EPA. This format revision will primarily affect the "Identification of plan--in part" sections, as well as the format of the SIP materials that will be available for public inspection at the EPA Regional Office and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA). This action, which only relates to rules applicable within six California air districts, is the fifth and final of a series of actions intended to change the format for the entire California SIP.

records.title: Announcement of the Intent To Award a Single-Source Cooperative Agreement to the Welcoming Initiative for Newcomers in San Diego, California
records.actor: Health and Human Services Department; Children and Families Administration
records.sourceText: The ACF, ORR announces the intent to award a single-source cooperative agreement in the amount of up to $3,500,000 to the Welcoming Initiative for Newcomers (WIN) in San Diego, California, for the next phase of the State Capacity and Readiness Initiative. Building on the nationwide baseline assessment and related readiness products completed under WIN's prior cooperative agreement, the proposed project will support an updated assessment of state capacity, support development of training and technical assistance resources, support for pilot implementation and learning, and engagement with states not participating in the pilots. The project will also identify service and capacity gaps and provide recommendations concerning additional grants, contracts, technical assistance, or other resources ORR may need to support a state-centered refugee resettlement model.

records.title: Drawbridge Operation Regulation; Wishkah River, Aberdeen, WA
records.sourceText: The Coast Guard is changing the operating schedule that governs the Puget Sound and Pacific railroad bridge (PS&P) across the Wishkah River, mile 0.1 in Aberdeen, WA. This rule will change the PS&P railroad bridge draw position to the fully closed-to-navigation position. Furthermore, this rule requires 24-hour notice for all drawbridge openings and a bridge operator will no longer be required to be on site.

records.title: Notice of Intent of Waiver With Respect to Land; Watertown Regional Airport, Watertown, South Dakota
records.sourceText: The FAA is considering a proposal to change approximately 4.99 acres of airport land from aeronautical use to non-aeronautical use and to authorize the sale of airport property located at the Watertown Regional Airport, Watertown, SD. The aforementioned land is not needed for aeronautical use. The subject property is made up of two parcels of airport property known as the Lot 4 (2.0 acres) and Dakota Tube (2.99 acres) parcels. These parcels are located north of the airport, along the east side of Airport Drive. Both properties are currently being used for industrial purposes and will continue to be used for the same purpose in the future.

records.title: Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC): Online Ordering and Transactions and Food Delivery Revisions To Meet the Needs of a Modern, Data-Driven Program
records.actor: Agriculture Department; Food and Nutrition Administration
records.sourceText: This final rule considers public comments submitted in response to the proposed rule to remove barriers to online ordering and internet-based transactions in the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) published on February 23, 2023. USDA FNA is issuing this regulatory action to support State innovation and develop and implement modernized systems, while underscoring program integrity. It allows for the use of new technologies to improve the WIC shopping experience while increasing access to healthy foods for WIC participants. This final rule also complements the Program's complete transition to electronic benefit transfer (EBT) by streamlining and modernizing certain WIC food delivery regulations to support current technology and future innovation, and introduces measures to support a modern, data-driven program that uses new technologies for food delivery.

records.title: Prohibiting Illegal Discrimination in Registered Apprenticeship Programs
records.sourceText: The Department of Labor (DOL or the Department) is issuing this final rule to remove the onerous and legally questionable affirmative action requirements that were previously imposed by the Department on Registered Apprenticeship program sponsors. This final rule also streamlines and simplifies nondiscrimination obligations for all program sponsors, while clarifying that sponsors are accountable for compliance with Federal and State nondiscrimination protections. It also makes conforming, technical changes to the Department's regulation that addresses Labor Standards for the Registration of Apprenticeship Programs.

records.title: U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System (IOOS®) Advisory Committee
records.actor: Commerce Department; National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
records.sourceText: NOAA is soliciting applications for membership on the United States Integrated Ocean Observing System Advisory Committee (the Committee), which is a Federal Advisory Committee. The Committee is mandated by the Integrated Coastal and Ocean Observation System Act of 2009 (the Act), part of the Omnibus Public Land Management Act of 2009 (Pub. L. 111-11), and the Coordinated Ocean Observations and Research Act of 2020 (Pub. L. 116-271) to provide advice to the NOAA Administrator and to the Interagency Ocean Observation Committee on the planning, integrated design, operation, maintenance, enhancement, and expansion of the United States Integrated Ocean Observing System (U.S. IOOS). NOAA is accepting applications for membership on the Committee to fill vacancies that will occur on September 14, 2027. NOAA encourages applications from individuals with expertise and/or experience in the following areas: coastal and ocean observing; data management and architecture; coastal and ocean modeling; Great Lakes; philanthropy; Non-Governmental Organization; scientific institutions (Academic); IOOS regional interests; State, local and tribal interests; blue economy; social science; public-private partnerships; marine technologies industries; ocean and coastal leadership; and other science-related fields.

records.title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Technical Corrections for 43 Wildlife and Plant Species on the Lists of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants
records.actor: Interior Department; Fish and Wildlife Service
records.sourceText: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), announce technical corrections for 43 wildlife and plant species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). For 7 wildlife species and 30 plant species that predominately occur in California and Nevada, we are revising the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and the List of Endangered and Threatened Plants ("the Lists") to reflect the current scientifically accepted taxonomy and nomenclature of these species. We are also making commensurate revisions to the applicable critical habitat sections. Further, for six wildlife species occurring within the United States and territories, we are correcting errors in the Lists made in previous publications. The taxonomic, nomenclatural, and orthographic revisions and the corrections of publication errors are editorial in nature and involve no substantive changes to the Lists or any applicable regulations.

records.title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Amendment 128 to the FMP for Groundfish of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area and Amendment 116 to the FMP for the Groundfish Fisheries of the Gulf of Alaska; Small Sablefish Release
records.actor: Commerce Department; National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
records.sourceText: The North Pacific Fishery Management Council (Council) submitted amendment 128 to the Fishery Management Plan (FMP) for Groundfish of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area (BSAI FMP) and amendment 116 to the FMP for Groundfish fisheries of the Gulf of Alaska (GOA FMP) to the Secretary of Commerce for review. If approved, these amendments would increase operational flexibility to allow vessels fishing for sablefish with fixed gear under the Individual Fishing Quota (IFQ) Program or Western Alaska Community Development (CDQ) Program to release sablefish and would revise the annual allocation process to account for sablefish discards. This action is intended to promote the goals and objectives of the Magnuson- Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act), the BSAI and GOA FMPs, and other applicable laws.

Specific Listing for 3-Chloromethcathinone, A Currently Controlled Schedule I Substance
records.sourceText: The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is establishing a specific listing and DEA Controlled Substances Code Number (drug code) for 1-(3-chlorophenyl)-2-(methylamino)propan-1-one (3- chloromethcathinone; 3-CMC) in schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). Although 3-chloromethcathinone is not specifically listed in schedule I of the CSA with its own unique drug code, it is a schedule I controlled substances in the United States because it is a positional isomer of 4-chloromethcathinone, which is a schedule I hallucinogen. Therefore, DEA is simply amending the schedule I hallucinogenic substances list in its regulations to separately include 3- chloromethcathinone.

records.actor: Health and Human Services Department; Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
records.sourceText: This final rule with comment period revises the Medicare Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and the Medicare Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) payment system for calendar year 2027 based on our continuing experience with these systems. We also describe the changes to the amounts and factors used to determine the payment rates for Medicare services paid under the OPPS and those paid under the ASC payment systems. In addition, this final rule with comment period updates and refines the requirements for the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and the Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Program. There are no changes to the Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program. We finalized the expansion of the prior authorization requirement to include additional Botulinum Toxin Injection services. We also finalized implementation of certain provisions of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, for off-campus outpatient departments of a provider. In addition, this final rule with comment period announces notices of closure of teaching hospitals and opportunities to apply for available slots. Additionally, we finalized the policy that hospital accrediting organizations (AOs) with deeming authority may assess compliance with certain Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) administrative requirements under 42 CFR 489.20 during accreditation and reaccreditation surveys.

records.title: Amendments to the “Small Business” and “Small Organization” Definitions for Investment Companies and Investment Advisers for Purposes of the Regulatory Flexibility Act
records.sourceText: The Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Commission" or the "SEC") is amending the definitions of "small business" and "small organization" (collectively, "small entities") that are used in connection with Commission rulemaking under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (the "Investment Company Act") and the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (the "Advisers Act"). These definitions concern regulatory requirements applicable to registered investment companies and business development companies (collectively, "funds") as well as investment advisers. The definitions are used specifically for purposes of the Regulatory Flexibility Act (the "RFA"), which requires the Commission to consider the impact of its regulations on small entities. The amendments are designed to modernize the definitions, by increasing certain asset-based thresholds, including a mechanism for periodic future inflation adjustments, and eliminating the threshold based on total assets for advisers. In connection with these amendments, the Commission is making conforming amendments to Form ADV as well as the rule that allows certain small SEC-registered advisers to apply for a continuing hardship exemption from making Advisers Act filings electronically.

The Tribe requested that the Bureau of Indian Affairs make three corrections to typographical errors it identified in its original Ordinance submission that was previously published in the Federal Register. First, Article I, Section 3 mistakenly identifies the Tribe's trust land as being in "Vallejo County"; the correct geographic description is "the City of Vallejo, Solano County, California." Second, Article I, Section 3(v) incorrectly uses the term "Indian county" instead of the correct statutory term "Indian country" as used in 18 U.S.C. 1154 and 1161. Third, Article VII, Section 1 contains a typographical error referring to "uncontested suits or actions"; the correct phrase is "unconsented suits or actions," accurately reflecting the Tribe's intent to preserve its sovereign immunity.

records.title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (25-3.5e)
records.sourceText: EPA is issuing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNURs require persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any of these chemical substances for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification; made an appropriate determination regarding that notification; and taken such actions as required by that determination.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
records.sourceText: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A318-111 and -112 airplanes; Model A319- 111, -112, -113, -114, -115, -131, -132, and -133 airplanes; Model A320-211, -212, -214, -216, -231, -232, and -233 airplanes; and Model A321-111, -112, -131, -211, -212, -213, -231, and -232 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of damage to the YZ-axis attachment points on airplanes equipped with certain overhead stowage compartments (OHSC) bins. Investigations showed that bushings, retainer rings, and pins had migrated from their original positions. This proposed AD would require a one-time inspection for discrepancies of affected OHSC bins and, depending on findings, accomplishment of applicable corrective actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Air Quality Implementation Plans; California; San Joaquin Valley; 2015 8-Hour Ozone Nonattainment Area Requirements; and California Consumer Products Regulations
records.sourceText: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve State implementation plan (SIP) revisions submitted by the State of California to meet Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act") requirements for the 2015 8-hour ozone national ambient air quality standards (NAAQS or "standards") in the San Joaquin Valley ozone nonattainment area ("San Joaquin Valley" or "SJV"). In this document, the EPA refers to these submissions collectively as the "SJV 70 ppb Ozone SIP." The EPA proposes to approve the SJV 70 parts per billion (ppb) Ozone SIP as meeting the applicable ozone nonattainment area requirements for emissions inventories, reasonably available control measures, attainment demonstration, rate of progress and reasonable further progress, motor vehicle emissions budgets, and enhanced monitoring. The EPA is also initiating the adequacy process for the budgets included in this SIP submission through this proposed rule. The EPA also proposes to approve two SIP revisions amending the SIP to incorporate changes reflecting updates to California Air Resources Board (CARB) Consumer Products Regulations and Method 310, which apply statewide and upon which the SJV 70 ppb Ozone SIP relies. These regulations concern emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOC) from antiperspirants, deodorants, consumer products, and aerosol coating products, and Method 310 is used to determine the VOC and reactive organic compounds content of these products. The EPA proposes to approve these regulations for purposes of the State's SIP under the CAA.

records.title: Air Plan Revisions; Arizona; Maricopa County Air Quality Department; New Source Review; Emission Reduction Credits
records.sourceText: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is taking final action to approve a revision to the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD or "Department") portion of the Arizona State Implementation Plan (SIP). This revision establishes a federally enforceable program allowing for the generation of emission reduction credits (ERCs) by retrofitting or replacing existing on-road vehicles with lower emitting vehicles while meeting other Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act") requirements. These ERCs are intended to be used as offsets for major stationary sources under the Department's Nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) program. The EPA is approving this SIP revision because we find that it meets the applicable CAA requirements.

records.title: Cost Standards and Procedures; Purchasing and Property Management
records.sourceText: This final rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC or Corporation) regulations governing cost allowability, prior approval requirements, and property and procurement standards applicable to LSC recipients. The final rule clarifies when recipients must obtain prior approval for expenditures of LSC funds; increases the monetary threshold for prior approval; clarifies the treatment of proceeds from fundraising activities supported with LSC funds; provides additional flexibility in LSC's review of prior approval requests; clarifies documentation requirements for prior approval requests; and revises the deadline and requirements for accounting for LSC funds invested in real estate. These amendments are intended to clarify existing requirements, reduce administrative burden, promote consistent oversight and enforcement, and strengthen accountability in the use of Federal funds.

records.title: Purchasing and Property Management
records.sourceText: This proposed rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC) definition of "capital improvement" by removing the threshold amount of LSC funds that must be expended on an improvement to real estate for the expenditure to qualify as a capital improvement. The proposed amendment would distinguish the definition of a capital improvement from the monetary thresholds required for prior approval; promote consistent tracking and oversight of LSC funds used for capital improvements; and strengthen accountability for LSC funds invested in recipients' real property.

records.title: Update and Clarification of the Passenger Facility Charge Regulations
records.sourceText: On September 27, 2023 FAA published a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) to amend its Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) regulations to implement congressionally mandated changes to an existing pilot program within the PFC program. FAA also proposed to reaffirm existing program requirements and update or remove obsolete references within the PFC regulations. Following publication of the NPRM and before FAA issued a final rule, the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (the 2024 Act) was signed into law on May 16, 2024. Several sections of the 2024 Act necessitate changes to PFC regulations or modifications to proposals made in the NPRM. As such, FAA now issues this supplemental proposal addressing: PFC turnback reductions; two new PFC-eligible projects; restrictions to PFC-eligible projects; FAA's timeline for review and acknowledgement of notice of intent (NOI) submissions; PFC streamlining review eligibility; and PFC submittal requirements. This proposal aligns with the requirements established by the 2024 Act.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; Pilatus Aircraft Ltd
records.sourceText: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-20-02, which applies to all Pilatus Aircraft Ltd. (Pilatus) Model PC-24 airplanes. AD 2025-20-02 requires incorporating a temporary revision into the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) for the affected airplanes, which revises the Abnormal Procedures Section. That action was considered an interim action. Since the FAA issued AD 2025- 20-02, updated software has been developed and instructions have been issued for installing the software. In addition, revised operational instructions have been issued that are applicable after installation of the updated software. This proposed AD would require installing the updated software and incorporating the applicable revised operational instructions into the AFM. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.sourceText: Notice is hereby given that the National Indian Gaming Commission (NIGC) has adopted its annual fee rates of 0.00% for tier 1 and 0.065% (.00065) for tier 2. While the rate for tier 1 remains the same, the tier 2 rate has been lowered from 0.08% to 0.065%. The tier 2 annual fee rate represents the lowest fee rate adopted by the NIGC since FY22. These rates shall apply to all assessable gross revenues from each gaming operation under the jurisdiction of the NIGC. If a tribe has a certificate of self-regulation, the fee rate on Class II revenues shall be 0.0325% (.000325) which is one-half of the annual fee rate. The annual fee rates are effective November 1, 2026, and will remain in effect until new rates are adopted. The NIGC has also adopted its fingerprint processing fee of $40 per card which is $4 lower than the current fee of $44 per card. A supplement was filed on October 13, 2026. The complaint, as supplemented, alleges violations of section 337 based upon the importation into the United States, the sale for importation, and the sale within the United States after importation of certain extrusion-coated magnet wire by reason of the infringement of certain claims of U.S. Patent No. 8,847,075 ("the '075 patent"), U.S. Patent No. 9,224,523 ("the '523 patent"), and U.S. Patent No. 10,210,966 ("the '966 patent"). records.title: Airworthiness Directives; MD Helicopters, LLC Helicopters
records.sourceText: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 90- 19-02, which applies to all MD Helicopters, LLC (type certificate previously held by McDonnell Douglas Helicopter Company) Model 369, 369A, 369D, 369E, 369F, 369FF, 369H, 369HE, 369HM, and 369HS, helicopters, that are equipped with a cargo hook. AD 90-19-02 requires replacing the overrunning clutch assembly and sprag assembly with airworthy parts and repetitively inspecting the sprag assembly, clutch inner and outer races of the overrunning clutch assembly. Since the FAA issued AD 90-19-02, after further analysis the FAA determined that additional helicopter models are affected by this unsafe condition. This proposed AD would expand the applicability and would require removing certain overrunning clutch assemblies and certain overrunning clutch subassemblies from service, installing or replacing parts, and reidentifying certain overrunning clutch assemblies, as applicable. This proposed AD would also require for certain model helicopters, revising the Airworthiness Limitations Section (ALS) of the existing aircraft maintenance manual (AMM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.sourceText: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or Department) issues this rule to revise the regulation implementing section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (section 504) as it applies to recipients of HHS funding (entitled "Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance," ("2024 Final Rule")), published on May 9, 2024. This rule clarifies that the Department interprets the statutory exclusion of "gender identity disorders not resulting from physical impairments" from the terms "individual with a disability" and "disability" set forth in our regulations to encompass "gender dysphoria not resulting from a physical impairment" for purposes of the regulation. This clarification is necessary to resolve ambiguity introduced in the preamble to the 2024 Final Rule and to ensure compliance with the best reading of the governing statute.

records.sourceText: This final rule revises the Conditions for Coverage for Organ Procurement Organizations (OPOs) to clarify outstanding procedural questions and provide additional operational flexibility for OPOs to achieve high performance resulting in the successful procurement, distribution, and transplantation of more life-saving organs. This rule revises definitions, revises the designation requirements for OPOs, clarifies when an OPO's service area is open for competition, and updates the process for appeals. We are committed to holding all OPOs accountable for their performance and this final rule does not revise the focus on improving the volume of donors and transplants assessed in the outcome measures or the tier structure used for re-certification and de-certification of OPOs.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; Embraer S.A. (Type Certificate Previously Held by Yaborã Indústria Aeronáutica S.A.; Embraer S.A.) Airplanes
records.sourceText: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-17-03, which applies to certain Embraer S.A. Model ERJ 190-100 STD, -100 LR, -100 IGW, and -100 ECJ airplanes; and Model ERJ 190-200 STD, -200 LR, and -200 IGW airplanes. AD 2024-17-03 requires revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-17-03, the FAA has determined that new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations are necessary. This proposed AD would continue to require certain actions in AD 2024-17-03 and would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
records.sourceText: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2024-25-09, which applies to certain The Boeing Company Model 757 airplanes. AD 2024-25-09 requires installing new relays and changing certain wire bundles leading to the power transfer unit (PTU) control valve. Since the FAA issued AD 2024-25-09, the FAA determined that the requirements bulletin mandated by AD 2024-25-09 contains errors. In some cases, those errors prevent the actions required by AD 2024-25-09 from being fully accomplished. In other cases, the errors would allow actions that could introduce new hazards affecting the operation and thus the availability of the PTU. This proposed AD would require, depending on the airplane configuration, installing new relays and new connectors, changing certain wire bundles, doing an operational test, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

The workshops are free; will be hosted in-person with select hybrid sessions offered virtually; and will require advance registration. Each workshop will be a full day and will cover a variety of best practices each session. PHMSA established the National LNG Center in 2023 pursuant to section 111 of the Protecting Our Infrastructure of Pipelines and Enhancing Safety (PIPES) Act of 2020 (Pub. L. 116-260), which directs the National LNG Center to advance Federal LNG expertise, serve as a repository of best practices, and facilitate collaboration among LNG stakeholders. records.actor: Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration
records.sourceText: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a final guidance titled "Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products." The guidance document provides recommendations to help assure the potency of human cellular therapy or gene therapy (CGT) products at all stages of the product lifecycle. FDA is recommending a comprehensive approach to potency assurance of CGT products that is grounded in quality risk management. For investigational products, we describe how to progressively implement a strategy for potency assurance during product development and provide additional considerations to help assure the potency of products that are undergoing rapid clinical development. For licensed products, we describe requirements for potency assurance, including testing required for lot release assays. The guidance announced in this notice finalizes the draft guidance of the same title issued on December 28, 2023.

records.title: Conforming Amendment Regarding the Criminal Law Technical Amendments Act of 2002
records.sourceText: The Criminal Law Technical Amendments Act of 2002 ("Technical Amendments Act") became law on November 2, 2002, as part of the 21st Century Department of Justice Appropriations Authorization Act. The Technical Amendments Act amended sections 401(d), 402(c), and 403 of the Controlled Substances Act by replacing outmoded fine amounts with a reference to title 18 of the United States Code in each place that a specific fine amount had appeared. In this rulemaking, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is amending its regulations to conform them to the statutory amendments made to the Controlled Substances Act by the Technical Amendments Act.

In the application, Perma-Fix seeks to amend and renew existing license, XW027/02, authorizing the export of radioactive waste to Germany. The NRC is providing notice of the opportunity to comment, request a hearing, and petition for leave to intervene on Perma-Fix's application. This action will renew the existing export license for an additional 5 years to expire on September 1, 2031, and amend the existing export license to decrease the total volume of waste from 800,000 kilograms (kg) to 200,000 kg, decrease the maximum activity of all shipments from 8.5 Terabecquerels (TBq) to 2.4 TBq, and add two radionuclides to the license.

Once finalized, the SNURs would require persons who intend to manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or process any of these chemical substances for an activity that is proposed as a significant new use by this rulemaking to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing that activity. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. Public harm is reasonably likely to occur if normal, non- emergency clearance procedures are followed. The approval of this data collection process is essential to ensure that the Review Choice Demonstration (RCD) for Home Health (HH) Services is expanded to California within the specified timeframe. A delay in the expansion means an extended time the public will be harmed through the continuation of significant fraud found in the traditional Medicare home health benefit in California through the waste of taxpayer money, a loss of funds from the Medicare Trust Funds that could have been used for truly needed care, paying for care that is never delivered, and beneficiaries potentially receiving non-medically necessary care. Improving Transparency Into Pharmacy Benefit Manager Fee Disclosure
records.actor: Labor Department; Employee Benefits Security Administration
records.sourceText: The Department is issuing a final regulation that will require providers of pharmacy benefit management services and affiliated providers of brokerage and consulting services to disclose information about their compensation to fiduciaries of large, self-insured group health plans subject to the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). Pharmacy spending is a major driver of overall healthcare costs for employers and is growing faster than medical and surgical spending. These disclosure requirements apply for purposes of ERISA's statutory prohibited transaction exemption for service arrangements under section 408(b)(2). These disclosures are needed so that fiduciaries can assess the reasonableness of contracts or arrangements with these service providers, including the reasonableness of the service providers' compensation. As directed in section 12 of President Trump's Executive Order 14273, Lowering Drug Prices by Once Again Putting Americans First, the Department is issuing this rule to improve employer health plan transparency into the direct and indirect compensation received by pharmacy benefit managers. This final rule will affect sponsors and other fiduciaries of large, self-insured group health plans and certain service providers to such plans.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; Diamond Aircraft Industries Inc. Airplanes
records.sourceText: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Diamond Aircraft Industries Inc. (DAI) Model DA 40, DA 40 F, and DA 40 NG airplanes. This AD was prompted by several reports of passenger door separation during flight. This AD requires revising the existing airplane flight manual (AFM) to provide the flight crew with revised operating limitations, emergency procedures, and normal operating procedures; inspecting the passenger door latching mechanism and safety hook mechanism areas and performing corrective action, as applicable; inspecting the safety hook, latching bolts, front and rear door guide blocks, canopy and passenger door warning light, carbon hinges, tension spring, retaining block, safety hook push button, latching mechanism spring, gas spring, and door frame; measuring the passenger door handle actuation force; modifying the airplane with placards; replacing the gas spring; and replacing the hook assembly, retaining block, door guide blocks, and door sealant if necessary. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
records.sourceText: The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2023-07- 09, which applied to certain The Boeing Company Model 747-400 and -8 series airplanes. AD 2023-07-09 required inspecting for wear of the transfer pump housing inlet check valves and transfer pump motor impeller inlet adapters for the horizontal stabilizer fuel tank and doing corrective actions, if necessary, and limited the installation of affected parts. This AD was prompted by the manufacturer developing further action to address the unsafe condition. This AD requires repetitive inspections for damage of the transfer pump housing inlet check valves and transfer pump motor impeller inlet adapters for the horizontal stabilizer fuel tank and applicable on-condition actions. This AD also limits the installation of affected parts under certain conditions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
records.sourceText: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report that, during production, certain sealant installations within the center wing fuel tank did not receive required visual and adhesion inspections. This AD requires a detailed inspection of certain sealant installations in the left, right, and center wing side-of-body areas, an adhesion test of the sealant, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Unleashing the Power of Unlicensed Ultra-Wideband Devices; Petition of Robert Bosch LLC for Amendment of the Part 15 Subpart F Ultra-Wideband Rules; and Petition of Alliance for Automative Innovation et al. To Amend Part 15 of the FCC's Rules To Permit the Operation of Certain Ultra-Wideband Devices
records.sourceText: The Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) proposes to update its rules for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) devices to reflect significant technological developments since the rules were first adopted in 2002. UWB technology has matured into a widely used, low-power enabler that supports applications in tracking, automation, precision location, health monitoring, athletic performance, and public safety. As capabilities of UWB have expanded, the existing rules have not kept pace with the technological change, resulting in an increasing number of waiver requests received by the Commission to authorize modern devices. The Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeks comment on revisions intended to modernize the UWB framework, provide greater flexibility for future applications, promote continued innovation, and ensure the protection of incumbent federal and non-federal spectrum users.

records.title: Dimethyl Sulfoxide in Pesticide Formulations; Exemptions From the Requirement of a Tolerance
records.sourceText: This regulation establishes exemptions from the requirement of a tolerance for residues of dimethyl sulfoxide (CAS Reg. No. 67-68-5) when used as an inert ingredient (solvent/cosolvent) in pesticide formulations applied to growing crops or to raw agricultural commodities after harvest, in pesticide formulations applied to animals, and in antimicrobial formulations applied to food-contact surfaces in public eating places, dairy-processing equipment, and food- processing equipment and utensils. Spring Regulatory Sciences on behalf of Gaylord Chemical Company, LLC submitted a petition to EPA under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FFDCA), requesting establishment of exemptions from the requirement of a tolerance. This regulation eliminates the need to establish maximum permissible levels for residues of dimethyl sulfoxide when used in accordance with the terms of those exemptions.

records.actor: Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration
records.sourceText: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a revised draft guidance for industry entitled "Essential Drug Delivery Performance Characteristics for Devices Intended to Deliver Drugs and Biological Products." This revised draft guidance revises and replaces the draft guidance entitled "Essential Drug Delivery Outputs Intended to Deliver Drugs and Biological Products" announced in the Federal Register on July 1, 2024 (89 FR 54470). In accordance with its mission of protecting, promoting, and advancing public health, this guidance addresses key aspects of drug delivery performance information for devices, and combination products that include device constituent parts, intended for delivery of a human drug, including a biological product (herein referred to as drug delivery devices). This guidance provides recommendations for development and organization of device drug-delivery performance information and data to improve the consistency of this information in applications and to facilitate transparency and predictability in development and regulatory review. The guidance is intended to facilitate and streamline development and lifecycle management of drug delivery devices.

records.title: Schedules of Controlled Substances: Placement of Centanafadine in Schedule III
records.sourceText: On July 24, 2026, the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a new drug application for Simtriyo (centanafadine) for the treatment of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in adults and pediatric patients aged 6 years and older, weighing at least 20 kg. The Department of Health and Human Services provided the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) with a scheduling recommendation to place centanafadine, chemically known as (1R,5S)-1- (naphthalen-2-yl)-3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane, in schedule III of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). In accordance with the CSA, as amended by the Improving Regulatory Transparency for New Medical Therapies Act, DEA is hereby issuing an interim final rule placing centanafadine, including its salts, isomers (whether optical, positional, or geometric), and salts of such isomers whenever the existence of such salts, isomers, and salts of isomers is possible in schedule III of the CSA.

records.actor: Health and Human Services Department; Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
records.sourceText: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), a component of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), announces the issuance of an Amended Order under Sections 361, 365, 368, and 369 of the Public Health Service Act, and associated implementing regulations, prohibiting the boarding of any person who is not otherwise subject to an exemption on any aircraft destined to the United States from a foreign country unless the person presents a signed attestation confirming the person has not been present in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) during the 21 days prior to boarding a flight to the United States. This Amended Order was issued on October 28, 2026, to become effective at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (EST) on November 3, 2026, and shall remain in effect through 11:59 p.m. EST on December 18, 2026. This Amended Order may be amended or rescinded prior to that time at the discretion of the Secretary or his designee.

records.title: Privacy Act of 1974; Matching Program
records.actor: Health and Human Services Department; Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
records.sourceText: In accordance with subsection (e)(12) of the Privacy Act of 1974, as amended, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), is providing notice of a computer matching program between CMS and participating State-Based Administering Entities (AEs), titled "Determining Eligibility for Enrollment in Applicable State Health Subsidy Programs Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act". The matching program supports eligibility determinations for enrollment in applicable State health subsidy programs under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA), including Qualified Health Plans (QHPs), Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), and Basic Health Programs (BHPs). The matching program also supports implementation of statutory requirements concerning Medicaid community engagement and the prevention of concurrent Medicaid enrollment in more than one State through the Multi-State Enrollment Prevention (MSEP) system.

records.title: Notice of Charter Renewal and Request for Nominations for the Great Lakes Advisory Board
records.sourceText: Notice is hereby given that the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has determined that, in accordance with the provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA), the EPA Great Lakes Advisory Board (GLAB) is a necessary committee which is in the public's interest. Accordingly, the Advisory Board will be renewed for an additional two-year period. In addition, EPA is seeking member nominations for the GLAB from qualified candidates to serve a two-year term. The purpose of the GLAB is to provide advice and recommendations to the EPA Administrator through the Great Lakes National Program Manager on matters related to the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative and on domestic matters related to the implementation of the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement. The Advisory Board's major objectives are to provide advice and recommendations on: Great Lakes protection and restoration activities; long term goals, objectives and priorities for Great Lakes protection and restoration; and other issues identified by the Great Lakes Interagency Task Force/Regional Working Group.

records.title: Air Plan Approval and Air Quality Designation; TN; Attainment Plan and Redesignation of the Sullivan County Nonattainment Area for the 2010 1-Hour Primary SO2 NAAQS
records.sourceText: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) is proposing to approve the State of Tennessee's attainment plan for the Sullivan County Nonattainment Area (Sullivan County Area or Area) for the 2010 Sulfur Dioxide (SO<INF>2</INF>) National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS). Additionally, the EPA is proposing to determine that the Area has attained the 2010 SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS and to approve Tennessee's maintenance plan for continued attainment. With these approvals, the EPA is proposing to approve Tennessee's comprehensive source-specific SO<INF>2</INF> permitted limits for two facilities in the Area, other control measures, and provisions for Reasonably Available Control Measures (RACM) and Reasonably Available Control Technology (RACT), reasonable further progress (RFP), a modeling demonstration of SO<INF>2</INF> attainment and maintenance, and to approve Tennessee's request to redesignate the Area from nonattainment to attainment of the 2010 SO<INF>2</INF> NAAQS. The EPA is taking these actions in accordance with the Clean Air Act (CAA or Act).

records.title: Fiftieth Update of the Federal Agency Hazardous Waste Compliance Docket
records.sourceText: Since 1988, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has maintained a Federal Agency Hazardous Waste Compliance Docket ("Docket") under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA). CERCLA requires EPA to establish a Docket that contains certain information reported to EPA by Federal facilities that manage hazardous waste or from which a reportable quantity of hazardous substances has been released. This document identifies the Federal facilities not previously listed on the Docket and identifies Federal facilities reported to EPA since the last update on April 23, 2026. In addition to the list of additions to the Docket, this document includes a section with revisions of the previous Docket list and a section of Federal facilities that are to be deleted from the Docket. Thus, the revisions in this update include one addition, one deletion, and eighteen corrections to the Docket since the previous update.

records.sourceText: Notice is hereby given that NMFS received three Hatchery and Genetic Management Plans (HGMPs) for hatchery programs rearing and releasing fall-run chum salmon in the Skagit River basin. The plans describe hatchery programs operated by the Sauk-Suiattle Indian Tribe, Swinomish Indian Tribal Community, Upper Skagit Indian Tribe, and Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife (WDFW), as co-managers. records.sourceText: The Commission will consider a Further Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (FNPRM) that would unlock 25 megahertz of prime mid-band spectrum for advanced commercial communications services, including terrestrial, direct-to-device (D2D), or a hybrid of both. The rules proposed in this item, if adopted, would enable the auctioning, licensing, and rapid development of the 1675- 1695 MHz and 2020-2025 MHz bands. In particular, the FNPRM would propose and seek comment on policies, service and technical rules, and coordination requirements for the 1675- 1695 MHz and 2020-2025 MHz bands.

records.title: Additional Reconsideration Standards of Performance for New, Reconstructed, and Modified Sources and Emissions Guidelines for Existing Sources: Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review
records.sourceText: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing amendments to the New Source Performance Standards and Emission Guidelines for the Crude Oil and Natural Gas Source Category to address additional concerns raised with prior regulatory amendments finalized in March 2024. Specifically, the EPA is proposing changes in response to certain petitions for reconsideration of the March 2024 amendments, changes based on policy decisions and supporting legal interpretations, and changes that correct and clarify the regulatory text of the new source performance standards and emission guidelines. First, the EPA proposes to rescind the Super Emitter Program. Second, the EPA proposes to subcategorize different types of well sites affected and designated facilities to address issues related to the requirements finalized in March 2024 for marginal well sites and conventional well sites. Third, the EPA proposes changes to address issues related to liquids unloading, process controllers, pumps, fugitive emissions, storage vessels, covers and closed vent systems, equipment leaks at gas plants, and associated gas. Fourth, the EPA proposes changes to certain requirements finalized in March 2024 related to control devices and to provide owners and operators the option to conduct optical gas imaging surveys according to Appendix K for gas processing facilities. Lastly, the EPA proposes changes to correct inadvertent errors and to clarify regulatory language.

records.sourceText: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2013-01-05, which applies to certain Airbus Helicopters (Eurocopter France) Model AS350B3 and EC130B4 helicopters. AD 2013-01-05 requires revising the Limitations section of the rotorcraft flight manual (RFM) supplement to reduce the starter generator operating current to 180 amperes (amps) and installing a placard in the instrument panel to indicate the revised limitation. Since the FAA issued AD 2013-01-05, the manufacturer determined the applicability needs to be revised to add helicopters equipped with certain part numbered starter generators and to remove helicopters with certain engines installed. This proposed AD would require revising the Limitations section of the RFM supplement of the existing RFM for the helicopter, to reduce the starter generator operating current to 180 amps and installing a placard in the instrument panel indicating the revised limitation. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Electronic Submission Template for Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) Applications; Draft Guidance for Sponsors and Food and Drug Administration Staff; Availability
records.actor: Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration
records.sourceText: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of the draft guidance titled "Electronic Submission Template for Investigational Device Exemption (IDE) Applications." FDA is issuing this draft guidance for sponsors submitting IDE applications to the Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) and Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER). It introduces those sponsors to the current publicly available resources and associated content developed to support IDE electronic submissions to FDA. This draft guidance, when finalized, is intended to represent one of several steps in meeting FDA's commitment to the development of electronic submission templates to serve as guided submission preparation tools for sponsors to improve submission consistency and enhance efficiency in the review process. This draft guidance is not final nor is it for implementation at this time.

records.title: Individualized Human Genome Editing Products: Considerations for BLA Submission and Postapproval Management; Draft Guidance for Industry; Availability
records.actor: Health and Human Services Department; Food and Drug Administration
records.sourceText: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or Agency) is announcing the availability of a draft document titled "Individualized Human Genome Editing Products: Considerations for BLA Submission and Postapproval Management." The draft guidance document provides recommendations for how an individualized human genome editing (GE) product that includes multiple product variants can be submitted in a single Biologics License Application (BLA). When finalized, this guidance will describe the FDA's current thinking on individualized GE products with respect to how to specify the extent of GE component variation in a BLA, how to add new product variants to the BLA after licensure, and related topics.

Denial of Motor Vehicle Defect Petition, DP26-004
records.actor: Transportation Department; National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
records.sourceText: This notice sets forth the reasons for the denial of a defect petition, DP26-004, submitted by Mr. Richard De Leon (the Petitioner) to NHTSA (the Agency) by letter received December 22, 2025. The petition requests that the Agency initiate a safety defect investigation into the hydraulic control unit (HCU) for the Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) on the Model Year (MY) 2010 Ford Fusion Hybrid. The petition alleges that an illuminated ABS malfunction indicator lamp (MIL) is associated with a failure of the ABS HCU, resulting in ABS malfunction, loss of traction and electronic stability control functions, and reduced braking performance on slippery road surfaces. After conducting a technical review of the petition and other information, the Agency concluded that the issues raised by the petition do not warrant a new defect investigation. Accordingly, the Agency denied the petition.

records.title: Voluntary Consensus Standards Update; Formaldehyde Emission Standards for Composite Wood Products
records.sourceText: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is publishing a final rule to update the incorporation by reference of several voluntary consensus standards in the Agency's formaldehyde standards for composite wood products regulations under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) due to the standards having been updated or superseded by the issuing organizations. These new standards primarily update test methods and product standards concerning composite wood products that use formaldehyde. EPA is also conforming these updated standards in the scope and definitional sections in the final rule and incorporating by reference a new small scale quality control chamber test method, similar to current methods already incorporated by reference. EPA is also removing one standard that was previously incorporated by reference to avoid redundancy, given that another identical, internationally recognized version of the standard is already incorporated by reference in this rule.

records.title: Television Broadcasting Services Elko, Nevada
records.sourceText: This document amends the Table of TV Allotments (table) of the Federal Communications Commission's (Commission) rules by substituting VHF channel 10 for UHF channel 20 at Elko, Nevada in response to a petition for rulemaking filed by Reno (KENV-TV) Licensee, Inc. (Licensee), the licensee of full power television station KENV-DT (KENV-DT or Station), Elko, Nevada. The Media Bureau (Bureau) previously granted a petition for rulemaking submitted by the Licensee to substitute UHF channel 20 for VHF channel 10 at Elko in the table, and subsequently granted a construction permit for its new channel. The Licensee states that it was unable to complete construction of the channel 20 facility by the deadline specified in the Station's construction permit. The Licensee filed the instant petition to amend the table to substitute VHF channel 10 for UHF channel 20 and allow KENV-DT to continue to operate on channel 10 at its licensed parameters and provide uninterrupted service to viewers. The staff engineering analysis finds that the proposal is in compliance with the Commission's principal community coverage and technical requirements, including the interference protection requirements. In support of its channel substitution request, the Licensee filed comments reaffirming its interest and stating that it commits to promptly take any and all steps that may be necessary to effectuate the channel substitution proposed in the petition. An individual commenter, Steven Quinn Singleton, also filed comments, which, for the reasons discussed in the Report and Order referenced below, the Bureau denied.

records.title: Requirement for Attestation for All Airline or Other Aircraft Passengers Arriving in the United States From Any Foreign Country and Controlled Free Pratique for Airlines Confirming That Such Passengers Have Not Been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in the Past 21 Days
records.actor: Health and Human Services Department; Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
records.sourceText: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), a component of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), announces it is issuing an Order under Sections 361, 365, 368, and 369 of the Public Health Service Act, and associated implementing regulations, prohibiting the boarding of any passenger who is not otherwise subject to an exemption on any aircraft destined to the United States from a foreign country unless the passenger presents a signed attestation confirming the passenger has not been present in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) during the 21 days prior to boarding a flight to the United States. This Order was issued on October 22, 2026, to become effective at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (EST) on November 3, 2026, and shall remain in effect through 11:59 p.m. EST on December 18, 2026. This Order may be amended or rescinded prior to that time at the discretion of the Secretary or his designee.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; CFM International, S.A. Engines
records.sourceText: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all CFM International, S.A. (CFM) Model CFM56-7B engines. This proposed AD was prompted by an event involving a CFM Model CFM56-7B26/3 engine where a fan blade separated and resulted in an engine in-flight shutdown (IFSD) with debris penetrating the fuselage, which caused a loss of pressurization and prompted an emergency descent. This proposed AD would require a visual inspection of the fan blades for findings considered not serviceable and, depending on the results of the inspection, replacement with a serviceable part and additional fan blade inspections. This proposed AD would also require sending the inspection results to CFM if any finding considered not serviceable is found. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
records.sourceText: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Model SA 365 N helicopters. This AD was prompted by reports of tightening torque loss on the input flange nut due to circular wear on the faces of the flange, the slip ring, and the input flange. This condition, if not addressed, could lead to degradation or jamming of the input roller bearings and loss of yaw control of the helicopter. This AD requires repetitive functional inspections (checks) and, depending on the results of the inspections, corrective actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters
records.sourceText: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3, EC635T2+, MBB-BK 117 C-2, and MBB-BK 117 D-2 helicopters. This AD was prompted by reports of cracks on the cable drum of the rescue hoist assembly. This AD requires repetitively inspecting the cable drum of certain rescue hoist assemblies for cracks and, depending on the results, replacing or repairing the cable drum of the rescue hoist assembly. This AD also prohibits the operation and the installation of an affected rescue hoist assembly on a helicopter, unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters
records.sourceText: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Model AS350B2, AS350B3, AS355N, AS355NP, and EC130B4 helicopters. This AD was prompted by a report of a release of the load on the cargo hook without manual release initiation by the pilot. This AD requires inspecting the load dropping control system, inspecting the manual release lever for free play, and, depending on the results, performing corrective actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
records.sourceText: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A330-941 airplanes. This AD requires the installation of a new FCPC standard and applicable concurrent modifications. This AD also prohibits the installation of certain parts. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes
records.sourceText: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 737-700, -700C, -800, and -900ER series airplanes. This AD was prompted by a leak through the form-in- place (FiP) gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel found during a leak check. This AD requires a detailed inspection of the left- and right-side FiP gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for correct sealant installation, a fluid leak test of the engine fuel shutoff valve access panels for any leak, and applicable on- condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes

This AD requires a detailed inspection of the FiP gasket at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for correct sealant installation, or a detailed inspection at the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for any damage on the preformed seal, depending on configuration; a fluid leak test of the engine fuel shutoff valve access panel for any leak; and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

records.title: Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes

EVS-TAP allows prescreened nationals of the People's Republic of China (PRC) to travel to the CNMI without a visa for temporary visits under specified conditions. records.sourceText: The International Trade Administration (ITA) announces the launch of the U.S. Resources Management Industry Listing (RMIL), or "industry listing." The RMIL is intended to identify U.S. companies operating in water and wastewater treatment; waste management and recycling, including critical minerals recycling; air quality measuring, monitoring and control; monitoring and instrumentation; weather and forecasting; and other resources management sectors for informational, engagement, and policy support purposes. The RMIL will provide a platform for U.S. companies to market their products and services, raising their visibility with international buyers seeking to purchase U.S. resources management solutions. The RMIL supports ITA's efforts to promote American technologies and services to overseas partners and position U.S. companies to compete for international project opportunities. Eligible companies may now apply to be listed in the RMIL. The industry listing will be published online and will be maintained by the International Trade Administration's Office of Energy and Environmental Industries.

Model SA226-T, SA226- AT, SA226-T(B), SA226-TC, SA227-AC (C-26A), SA227-AT, SA227-BC (C-26A), SA227-PC, SA227-CC, SA227-DC (C-26B), and SA227-TT (300) airplanes. records.title: Commercial Driver's License: PAM Transport, Inc.; Application for Exemption
records.actor: Transportation Department; Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration
records.sourceText: FMCSA requests public comment on PAM Transport Inc.'s (PAM) application for an exemption from the requirement that a holder of a commercial learner's permit (CLP) who has successfully passed the commercial driver's license (CDL) skills test but not yet been issued CDL credentials be accompanied by a CDL holder in the front seat, while the commercial motor vehicle (CMV) is driven by the CLP holder. PAM states that the CDL holder would remain in the CMV while the CLP holder is driving, but not necessarily in the passenger seat of the vehicle. FMCSA is required by statute to publish a notice explaining each exemption request. This notice does not indicate what decision FMCSA will ultimately reach on the request. After reviewing the application, safety analyses, and public comments submitted, FMCSA will grant or deny the exemption.

records.title: Special Conditions: Embraer S.A. Model ERJ 190-400 Airplane; Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System
records.sourceText: This action proposes special conditions for the Embraer S.A. (Embraer) Model ERJ 190-400 series airplane. This airplane will have a novel or unusual design feature when compared to the state of technology envisioned in the airworthiness standards for transport category airplanes. This design feature is a functionality known as the Embraer Enhanced Takeoff System (E\2\TS). The applicable airworthiness regulations do not contain adequate or appropriate safety standards for this design feature. These proposed special conditions contain the additional safety standards that the Administrator considers necessary to establish a level of safety equivalent to that established by the existing airworthiness standards.

records.title: Safety Zone; Southern California Annual Firework Events for the Los Angeles-Long Beach Captain of the Port Zone
records.sourceText: The Coast Guard is proposing to amend the Southern California Firework Events for Los Angeles-Long Beach Captain of the Port Zone Annual Safety Zones. The Coast Guard proposes eight new events to be added, thirteen events to be updated, and two events removed. The safety zones are needed to protect waterways users and keep them clear of potentially harmful debris within the fallout zone. This proposed rulemaking would prohibit persons and vessels from being in the safety zone unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port Los Angeles-Long Beach. We invite your comments on this proposed rulemaking.

records.title: Bipartisan Safer Communities Act of 2022-Criteria for National Instant Criminal Background Check System (“NICS”) Background Checks of Firearm Handlers
records.sourceText: The United States Department of Justice ("Department") is amending several of its regulations pertaining to the National Instant Criminal Background Check System ("NICS" or "system") of the Federal Bureau of Investigation ("FBI") to authorize Federal Firearm Licensees ("FFLs" or "licensees") to use NICS for purposes of voluntarily conducting employment background checks relating to certain current or prospective FFL employees. This final rule describes in more detail how, upon its effective date, FFLs will be able to conduct "firearm handler background checks" ("FHCs") of "eligible employees."

records.title: Hazardous Materials: Harmonization With International Standards

records.sourceText: PHMSA proposes to update the Hazardous Materials Regulations to adopt certain international regulations and standards related to proper shipping names, hazard classes, packing groups, special provisions, packaging authorizations, air transport quantity limitations, and vessel stowage requirements. These proposed amendments are intended to maintain consistency with the latest international regulations and standards, to reduce costs to entities or individuals within the United States, and to lower the cost of regulations on the U.S. economy.

records.title: Implementation of HAVANA Act of 2021
records.sourceText: On April 19, 2024, the Department of Justice published an interim final rule to implement the HAVANA Act of 2021. No comments were received on the interim final rule. The HAVANA Act authorizes agency heads to provide payments to certain individuals who have incurred qualifying injuries to the brain. records.title: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards; Modernization of FMVSS No. 108 To Accommodate ADS-Equipped Vehicles
records.actor: Transportation Department; National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
records.sourceText: NHTSA is proposing to amend Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 108, "Lamps, reflective devices, and associated equipment." The proposed updates to the standard are intended to remove unnecessary requirements and to provide design flexibility without impact on vehicle safety. The first two proposed changes would amend the test voltage specification for integral beam type headlamps and remove requirements that apply to vertical headlamp arrangements. Further proposed changes address vehicles equipped with Automated Driving Systems (ADS) that do not have manually operated driving controls. Those modifications would limit the application of certain requirements for manually operated turn signal, hazard warning signal, and beam switching controls to vehicles with manually operated driving controls. The changes are intended to address regulatory burdens and costs associated with equipment that does not fulfill the same purpose or provide safety benefits in an ADS-equipped vehicle without manually operated driving controls as in a vehicle with such controls. The changes would also narrow certain requirements for telltales to vehicles with manually operated driving controls and incorporate the term "telltale" where appropriate throughout the standard. Finally, a proposed addition to the standard would allow cyan-colored ADS marker lamps as optional motor vehicle lighting equipment in ADS-equipped vehicles.

records.title: Closed Captioning of Video Programming
records.sourceText: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) exempts video programmers for public, educational, and governmental access (PEG) channels from the requirement to register with the Commission and to certify captioning compliance if the PEG video programmers provide video programming exclusively to PEG channels that are exempt from closed captioning requirements. Additionally, providers of PEG programming are relieved of filing obligations if the administrators of non-exempt PEG channels certify compliance for programming carried on such channels. The Commission similarly exempts providers of programming carried on nonbroadcast networks for distribution by a cable operator or other multichannel video programming distributor (MVPD) from certifying when the nonbroadcast network itself certifies that it is exempt or that all programming comprising the network's linear line-up is either exempt from or compliant with the closed captioning rules.

records.title: Modernizing the Ability of Consumers To Control Robocalls
records.sourceText: In this document, the Commission seeks comment on measures to ensure that the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) rules that govern robocalls continue to evolve with changes in technology and industry practices. Specifically, we seek comment on reducing the timeframe callers must honor revocation requests, requirements for two- way texting functionality, requiring a revoke all method, and the treatment of affiliates.

records.title: Enhancing the Ability of Consumers To Control the Robocalls
records.sourceText: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) modifies rules to ensure that consumers can revoke consent for robocalls they no longer wish to receive while continuing to receive those they still want. We also modernize our rules to ensure that consumers have clear, simple, and automated ways to revoke consent while streamlining callers' ability to process revocations. Specifically, we allow callers to interpret a revocation request as applying only to the specific category of informational robocalls to which the revocation was directed, allow callers to designate an exclusive means to revoke consent, and amend the exemption from the consent requirement for financial institutions to allow them to more easily alert customers to fraudulent activity on their account. In addition, we delegate authority to the Consumer and Governmental Affairs Bureau (CGB) in consultation with the Enforcement Bureau (EB) to review our robocall rules to ensure that those rules are clear and easy to read.

records.sourceText: The Department of the Treasury (Treasury) is issuing this proposed rule to carry out the purposes of section 1001 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (the Act or the ROAD Act). Section 1001 of the ROAD Act prohibits large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, subject to certain exceptions. The proposed rule would clarify certain terms relevant to those restrictions, including "large institutional investor"; clarify the application of certain exceptions from the statutory prohibition; and clarify the statutory enforcement mechanism. The proposed rule is intended to provide clarity to market participants and other stakeholders on the application of the statute before the effective date of the ROAD Act.

records.title: Clarification on Department of Justice and Department of Education Guidance Documents Regarding Federal Nondiscrimination Laws
records.sourceText: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) and U.S. Department of Education (ED) (the Departments) are issuing this document to clarify that seven guidance documents issued jointly by the Departments are not enforceable. In addition, the Departments plan to revisit these guidance documents in light of the Supreme Court's decision in Loper Bright Enters. v. Raimondo, 603 U.S. 369, 400 (2024), to assess whether they are consistent with the single best meaning of the relevant statutory text. The Departments will not rely upon these guidance documents in their enforcement of federal civil rights laws, including Titles IV and VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (Title IV and Title VI), 42 U.S.C. 2000c et seq. and 2000d et seq., the Equal Educational Opportunities Act of 1974 (EEOA), 20 U.S.C. 1701-1720, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA), 42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq., and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (Section 504), 29 U.S.C. 794.

L- BAR records included appeals of U.S. Department of State (the "Department") determinations related to loss of U.S. nationality the denial of an application for a U.S. passport, or the revocation of a U.S. passport. This AD was prompted by reports of in-flight "Engine Degraded" messages from the engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) due to corrosion of the variable geometry (VG) system actuator. This AD requires removing certain electronic engine control (EEC) full authority digital electronic control (FADEC) software versions from service and installing an updated EEC FADEC software that is eligible for installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
